title: US Weighs Extending the Blockade to Cloud Computing as CXMT's Fifth-Generation Memory Platform Narrows the Gap With Samsung and SK Hynix
subhead: Washington is considering restricting the cloud networks Chinese firms use to train frontier models on Nvidia hardware leased through proxies abroad — a prospective choke point SCMP calls the steepest since the chip bans — while China's CXMT pushes a new fifth-generation DRAM process and both sides' top trade officials open summit-teaser talks in New York on AI, tariffs and critical minerals.

sections.heading: Cloud Computing in the Crosshairs: Washington Weighs Restricting the Last AI Training Lane
sections.body: The South China Morning Post reports that US officials are weighing restrictions on cloud computing, which would extend the tech blockade into the territory Chinese developers have used to quietly keep pace after the advanced-chip bans. Chinese firms, according to a Shenzhen broker cited by SCMP, have set up proxy entities in foreign jurisdictions to lease Nvidia server space in data centers across Southeast Asia, Japan and the Middle East, training models on cutting-edge processors outside US reach under contracts signed by non-Chinese entities. SCMP frames the move as China's AI sector facing its 'most severe choke point since the chip bans' if it lands.
sections.whyItMatters: Chips were only half the fight — the cloud has been the workaround. Extending controls to remote compute access would force Chinese frontier labs to lean harder on domestic silicon and smuggled hardware, testing the limits of the export-control regime itself.

sections.heading: CXMT Debuts a Fifth-Generation Memory Platform, Closing in on Samsung and SK Hynix
sections.body: SCMP reports that Chinese DRAM maker CXMT said it adopted its new-generation technology platform, dubbed G5, for mass production, narrowing the manufacturing-node lead of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. CXMT says it reached an 11.95-nanometre threshold using 'quadruple exposure' technology, close to the 'world's most advanced mass production memory platforms,' with wafer die output up at least 50 per cent. It also showed two mass-produced LPDDR5X chips with 24-gigabit capacity, a 50 per cent jump over the prior generation.
sections.whyItMatters: CXMT previously crossed into HBM3E-class memory; this move attacks the mainstream DRAM node gap directly. A Chinese supplier at near-parity on process nodes changes the pricing and security calculus for the entire memory market, and for the AI buildout that consumes it.

sections.heading: Bessent, He and Greer Open Summit-Teasers in New York on AI, Tariffs and Critical Minerals
sections.body: Reuters reports US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer met in New York on Sunday to line up potential agreements ahead of this week's Trump-Xi summit in Washington. Talks at JPMorgan Chase's Manhattan headquarters were set to run all day, covering a US-China trade truce that expires Nov. 10, Chinese rare-earth magnet and critical-mineral flows, and AI guardrails after reported security breaches involving AI models. Bessent told reporters he expected 'focused, fulsome and constructive talks.' Analyst Anna Ashton of Ashton Intelligence said both sides likely want 'a show of deliverables' for a presidential summit, but did not expect 'some sort of breakthrough,' with the status quo the likely best-case outcome.
sections.whyItMatters: The agenda links AI safety, critical minerals and tariff deadlines into a single negotiation, meaning the summit's outcome — however incremental — will set the near-term tone for export controls, rare-earth policy and the November 10 truce expiry all at once.

sections.heading: Chinese Academy of Sciences Charts a Sub-3nm Path With Older DUV Tools
sections.body: SCMP reports that researchers at the state-backed Chinese Academy of Sciences have established an early gate-all-around (GAA) device development path using deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, per Taiwanese media Digitimes, citing a speech by Ye Tianchun of the academy's Institute of Microelectronics. Ye said the institute had completed early integration for stacked nanosheet-channel GAA CMOS transistors using DUV tools, describing a 'new early-stage MOS transistor process path for China's sub-3-nm advanced manufacturing.' CAS is barred from buying ASML's advanced EUV machines under US sanctions.
sections.whyItMatters: This is early-stage research, not production, but it shows China actively pursuing an alternative sub-3nm route without EUV — the same pattern as multi-patterning DUV breakthroughs elsewhere, and a sign that sanctions push the search for process workarounds rather than stopping it.

sections.heading: Hygon Moves From Data Centers Into Robotics as Physical-AI Chips Multiply
sections.body: SCMP reports that Chinese chipmaker Hygon Information Technology will release a new chip targeting physical-world applications including robotics, expanding beyond data centers, with a product launch slated for Tuesday in Shenzhen. The chip, an iteration of the company's CPU1000 series, targets 'low-power, embedded and edge computing requirements' for robotics, machine vision and intelligent manufacturing, with the event sloganeered 'Let computing power reach the physical world.' Separately, Nikkei Asia reports Japan will assign unique IDs to industrial machinery across producers to collect physical-AI data, building a shared dataset for training robots and embodied systems.
sections.whyItMatters: China's domestic chip ecosystem is broadening from servers into the edge where humanoids and industrial robots run, while Japan moves to standardize how physical-AI training data is gathered — two parallel bets on embodied computing as the next compute frontier beyond the data center.

sections.heading: North Korean Hackers Weaponize Fake AI Job Interviews to Steal Crypto
sections.body: Nikkei Asia reports that North Korean hackers compromised devices in more than 100 countries through fake online job interviews, tricking applicants into running malware used to steal cryptocurrency. Japanese authorities say the actors gained access to over 30,000 devices worldwide between late 2025 and July 2026, with more than $10 million in cryptocurrency stolen in attacks targeting tech workers. The lures use AI-assisted interview setups to appear legitimate.
sections.whyItMatters: This is a targeted, AI-enabled social-engineering campaign against the tech workforce that finances itself through stolen crypto — a concrete example of how state actors now use AI tools to scale a classic insider-access attack.

sections.heading: Japanese Capital Fills the AI Funding Gap: Nippon Life Plans $12.7bn for Data Centers
sections.body: Nikkei Asia reports Nippon Life Insurance plans to invest 2 trillion yen ($12.7 billion) in infrastructure financing, including US data center construction. The insurer's move comes as rising prices for semiconductors, servers and other hardware make it harder to secure financing for data center buildout, with Japanese financial institutions stepping in to fill the gap. The report follows other Japanese AI-hardware plays this month, from battery suppliers to chip-equipment makers expanding abroad.
sections.whyItMatters: The physical AI buildout is now straining financing as hardware costs climb, and patient Japanese capital is emerging as a source for US-centric compute infrastructure — another route by which the data-center boom is being capitalized, and partly anchored, overseas.

bottomLine: The day's defining development is that the US-China compute fight is moving from chips to the cloud: Washington is weighing restrictions on the overseas Nvidia server capacity Chinese firms have been leasing through proxies, which SCMP describes as the steepest choke point since the chip bans. In parallel, CXMT pushed its fifth-generation DRAM platform into mass production at 11.95nm and 24-gigabit chips, narrowing the node gap with Samsung and SK Hynix, while CAS sketched a sub-3nm GAA path using blocked EUV alternatives. Bessent, He and Greer opened summit prep in New York tying AI guardrails, rare-earth flows and the November 10 truce expiry into one negotiation, even as Hygon moved into robotics chips, Nippon Life committed $12.7 billion to US data-center financing, and North Korean actors used fake AI job interviews to strip over $10 million in crypto from tech workers. The throughline: the race is now being fought at the cloud layer, the memory layer and the physical-AI edge simultaneously, with financing and diplomacy following close behind.
sources: SCMP (cloud computing restrictions; CXMT G5 platform; CAS sub-3nm DUV path; Hygon robotics chip), Reuters via Nikkei Asia (Bessent-He-Greer talks), Nikkei Asia (North Korean AI job-interview hacks; Nippon Life data-center financing; Japan physical-AI data)
